data: {"body":"Abut Tufail said he saw God’s messenger going round the House, touching the corner with a crooked stick which he had, and kissing the crooked stick. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2462"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Umama told that ‘Umar b. al-Khattab put on a new garment and said, “Praise be to God who has clothed me with something with which to cover my nakedness and adorn myself in my lifetime.” He then told that he had heard God's messenger say that if anyone who puts on a new garment says, “Praise be to God who has clothed me with something with which to cover my nakedness and adorn myself in my lifetime,” then takes the old garment and gives it as sadaqa, he will be in God’s protection, guardianship and shelter both when alive and when dead. \nAhmad, Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted it, Tirmidhi saying this is a gharib tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4191"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"‘Umair client of Abul Lahm said:

I was present at Khaibar along with my masters who spoke about me to God's Messenger, telling him that I was a slave. He ordered that I should have a sword girded on me, and I was trailing it.* He then ordered that I should be given some inferior goods. I submitted to him an invocation with which I used to treat people who were possessed and he ordered me to reject part of it and retain part. 

*Either because he was a small man, or because he was young.

Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud transmitted it, but the latter's version ended at “goods”.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3842"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Mas'ud reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Shedding of blood will be the first matter about which judgment will be given on the day of resurrection.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Retaliation · Hadith 3313"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Amr b. al-'As reported the Prophet as saying. \"Being killed in God’s path will cover up everything but debt.\" \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3645"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that God’s messenger entered on the day of the Conquest of Mecca wearing a black turban, but not wearing the ihram. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2605"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Talq b. ‘Ali said; we went out as a deputation to God’s Messenger and swore allegiance to him and prayed along with him. We told him that we had a church in our land, and we asked him for some of the leavings of the water he used for ablution. He called for water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth, then poured it out for us into a skin vessel, and gave us the following command, “Go away, and when you come to your land break down your church, sprinkle this water on its site, and use it as a mosque.\" We told him that our land was distant, the heat severe, and that the water would evaporate, to which he replied, “Add some water to it, for it will only bring more good to it.”\n\nNasa'i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 667"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Zaid b. Thabit said that God’s Messenger made an apartment of reed mats in the mosque and prayed in it for some nights until people gathered round him. One night when they missed his voice and thought he had gone to sleep, some of them began to clear their throats in order that he might come out to them, so he said, “What I have seen you doing has continued to be your practice, so that I have been afraid that it might be prescribed for you, and if it were prescribed for you you would not fulfil it. You people should therefore pray in your houses, for, with the exception of the prescribed prayer, the most excellent prayer a man observes is that which he observes in his house.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1227"}

data:
{"body":"Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari told of a man who came to the Prophet and
said, “My camel has become jaded, so give me a mount.” On his replying that he had none, a man said, “Messenger of God, I can guide him
to one who will give him a mount.” God’s messenger then said, “He
who guides to what is good will have a reward equivalent to that of him
who does it.” Muslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Knowledge · Hadith 200"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ali said that Khadija asked the Prophet about two children of hers who had died in the pre-Islamic period and God’s messenger replied, “They are in hell.” Then when he saw her look of disapproval he said, “If you saw their position you would hate them.” She asked, “Messenger of God, what about my son whom I had from you?” He replied, “He is in paradise.” Then God’s messenger said, “The believers and their children are in paradise and the polytheists and their children are in hell.” Then God’s messenger recited, “Those who believe and whose offspring have followed them.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 110"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas reported God’s messenger as saying, “This is an ‘umra which we have treated as a complete observance, so those who have no sacrificial animals may come completely out of the sacred state, for the ‘umra has become incorporated in the hajj till the day of resurrection.\" \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2449"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s Messenger as saying, \"Spoils were not lawful for anyone before us, that being because God saw our weakness and incapacity and made them allowable for us.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3822"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Umar told that when a man asked God’s messenger what clothing one who was on pilgrimage should wear, he said, “Do not wear shirts, turbans, trousers, garments with head coverings, or  shoes, unless one cannot get sandals and wears shoes, in which case he must cut them to come below the ankles; and you must not wear clothing which has any dye of saffron or wars (A plant of a yellow colour in the Yemen, like sesame. The word is also used for the colouring matter which is shaken out when the dower opens) \n\nBukhari and Muslim. Bukhari added in a version, “A woman who is on pilgrimage must not be veiled, or wear gloves.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2565"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Imran b. Husain told that when the slave of some poor people cut off the ear of a slave of some rich people, and his people came to the Prophet telling him that they were poor, he imposed no compensation on them. \n\nAbu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Retaliation · Hadith 3363"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s Messenger as saying, “No woman who has used incense maybe present with us at the last evening prayer.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1000"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Nafi’ said on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar that the Prophet used to make his riding-beast kneel between him and the qibla and pray facing it. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.) Bukhari added that Nafi' asked Ibn ‘Umar, saying, “Tell me what happened when the camels moved away,” to which he replied, “He used to take the saddle, put it straight, and pray facing the back of it.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 723"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Al-Hakam b. Sufyan said that when the Prophet passed water he performed ablution and sprinkled his penis. \n\nAbu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 336"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir told of hearing God’s messenger say, “When you hear the barking of dogs and the braying of asses at night seek refuge in God from the accursed devil, for they see what you do not see. Do not go out much when there are few people about, for God who is great and glorious scatters abroad such of His creatures as He wishes at night* Shut the doors, making mention of God's name, for the devil does not open a door which has been shut accompanied by mention of God’s name. Cover up jars, invert vessels and tie up buckets.”\n\nIt is transmitted in Sharh as-sunna.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4125"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha told that when Sauda became old she said, “Messenger of God, I appoint to ‘A'isha the day you visit me” (Cf. the last tradition in this chapter).  So God’s Messenger allotted two days to ‘A’isha, hers and Sauda’s. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3102"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said that when God’s messenger went out to the place of prayer on the day of sacrifice, or on the day when the fast was broken, he came upon some women and said, \"Give alms, you women folk, for I have been shown that you will be the majority of the inhabitants of hell.” They asked, “For what reason, messenger of God?” He replied, “You are greatly given to abuse, and you are ungrateful to your husbands. Among women who are deficient in intelligence and religion I have not seen anyone more able to remove the understanding of a prudent man than one of you.” They asked, “What is the deficiency of our religion and our intelligence, messenger of God?” He replied, “Is not the testimony of a woman equivalent to half the testimony of a man?” They said, “Yes.” Remarking that that pertained to the deficiency of her intelligence, he asked, “Is it not the case that when she menstruates she neither prays nor fasts?” When they replied, “Yes,” he said, “That pertains to the deficiency of her religion.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 18"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa'id and Abu Huraira reported God's messenger as saying, “Recite to those of you who are dying, ‘There is no god but God. ’ ” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1534"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas told that Abu Talha and the Prophet were both using one shield. Abu Talha was a good archer, and when he shot the Prophet looked over and watched where his arrows went. \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3702"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Ja'far said the Prophet saw a dwarf and prostrated himself. \n\nDaraqutni transmitted it in mursal form. Sharh as-sunna has the same wording as al-Masabih.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1415"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said he used to sell camels at an-Naqi‘for dinars and take dirhams for them, and sell for dirhams and take dinars for them. He went to the Prophet and mentioned that to him, and he replied, “There is no harm in taking them at the current rate so long as you do not separate leaving something still to be settled.” \n\nTirmidhi, Abu Dawud, Nasa’i and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2752"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira said God’s messenger cursed the man who dressed like a woman and the woman who dressed like a man. \nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4282"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir reported God’s Messenger as saying, “He who dies leaving a will has died following a path and a sunna, he has died piously and testifying to the true faith, and he has died with his sins forgiven.”\n\nIbn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Inheritance and Wills · Hadith 2952"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Musa said that God's Messenger cursed those who separated a parent from his child and a brother from his brother. \n\nIbn Majah and Daraqutni transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3238"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Amir b. Rabi'a said that they prayed the morning prayer behind ‘Umar b. al-Khattab and that he recited slowly in both rak'as Sura Yusuf and Sura al-Hajj (Al-Qur’an; 22). When someone remarked that he must have begun the prayer at break of day he replied that that was so. \n\nMalik transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 810"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abu Huraira reported God’s Messenger as saying, \"Do not turn against your fathers, for he who turns against his father has become an infidel.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3183"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Amr b. Shu'aib, quoting his father on the authority of his grandfather, said that a nomadic Arab came to the Prophet and asked him about ablution. He demonstrated it, performing each detail three times and then said, “This is how ablution should be performed. If anyone does more than this, he has done wrong, transgressed, and done wickedly.” \n\nNasa’i and Ibn Majah transmitted it, and Abu Dawud transmitted something to the same effect.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 385"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani told that he said, “Prophet of God, we are in a land belonging to folk who are people of the Book, so may we eat out of their vessels? In a hunting region I hunt with my bow, my dog which is not trained and my dog which is trained, so what is right for me?” He replied, “Regarding what you have mentioned about the vessels of the people of the Book, if you can get anything else do not eat out of them, but if you cannot, wash them and eat out of them. Eat what you catch with your bow when you have mentioned God’s name; eat what you catch by your trained dog when you have mentioned God’s name; and eat what you catch by your untrained dog when you are present at the kill.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Game and Animals Which May Be Slaughtered · Hadith 3901"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Mas'ud told of a man coming to the Prophet and saying, “Messenger of God, I sported with a woman on the outskirts of Medina, and I got what I wanted from her short of having intercourse with her. Now here I am, so decide what you wish about me.” ‘Umar said to him, “God has concealed this about you. Would that you had kept it to yourself!” Ibn Mas'ud said that the Prophet gave no reply, so the man got up and went away. Then the Prophet sent a man after him to summon him, and he recited this verse to him. “And observe the prayer at the two ends of the day and the neighbouring parts of the night, for good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder to those who remember (Al-Qur’an, 11:114).” One of the people asked, “Prophet of God, does this refer to him in particular?” He replied, “No, it refers to all men.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 532"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Malik b. al-Huwairith said that he and a cousin of his came to the Prophet, who said, “When you two are on a journey, you should call the adhan and repeat the iqama, then the older of you should act as imam.” \n\nThis is how Bukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 635"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas reported God’s messsenger as saying that if anyone asks God for paradise three times, paradise will say, ‘‘O God, bring him into paradise;” and if anyone asks for protection from hell three times, hell will say, \"O God, grant him protection from hell.” \n\nTirmidhi and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2371"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"A companion of God’s Messenger reported him as saying, “When two people come together to issue an invitation accept that of the one who lives nearer you, but if one of them comes before the other accept the invitation of the one who comes first.” \n\nAhmad and Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3095"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that he, meaning God’s Messenger, would sleep in the early part of the night and keep awake in the latter part. If he then wished intercourse with his wife he satisfied his desire, and then went to sleep. If he was sexually defiled when the first call to prayer was made, he would get up and pour water on it, but if not, he performed the ablution for the prayer and then prayed two rak'as. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1163"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said, “When God’s Messenger grew old and was ill, he mostly prayed sitting.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1135"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas told how the Prophet used to say, ‘‘Keep in alignment, keep in alignment, keep in alignment, for by Him in whose hand my soul is, I can see you behind me just as I see you in front of me.\" \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1038"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Anas said:

When the Prophet took us out on an expedition against a people he did not set out with us till the morning. He would look at them, and if he heard a call to prayer he refrained from them, but if he did not hear any he attacked them. We went out to Khaibar and reached them by night, but when the morning came and he heard no call to prayer he mounted. I mounted behind Abu Talha and my foot was touching God’s Prophet’s They came out to us with their large baskets and their spades, and when they saw the Prophet they said, “Muhammad, by God, Muhammad and the army," and went for refuge to the fortress. When God's Messenger saw them he said, “God is most great, God is most great. Khaibar has fallen.1 When we alight in the courtyard of a people it is an evil morning for those who have been warned."2 

1.	 Or, 'May Khaibar fall. 
2.	 Cf. Al-Qur'an; 37:177.

(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3768"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that God's Messenger ordered that a mosque be built in a residential district and that it be cleaned and perfumed. \n\nAbu Dawud, Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 668"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar reported God’s messenger as saying, \"Supplication is beneficial regarding things which have happened and things which have not happened, so devote yourselves to supplication, servants of God.\"\n\nTirmidhi transmitted it, and Ahmad transmitted it from Mu'adh b. Jabal. Tirmidhi said this is a gharib tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2137"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"She reported the Prophet as saying, “Those who will receive the severest punishment on the day of resurrection will be they who imitate what God has created.” \n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4308"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas said that a man of Kilab asked the Prophet about hiring a stallion to cover a female and he forbade him; but when he said, \"Messenger of God, we lend a stallion to cover a female and are given a present,\" he gave him licence to accept a present. \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2747"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"He said:

We used to employ people to till land for a share of its produce* and see no harm in it till Rafi' b. Khadij asserted that the Prophet forbade it, so we abandoned it on that account.

Muslim transmitted it.

* Mukhabir. From this comes the verbal noun mukhabara. See p. 607.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2850"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s Messenger as saying, “When one of your prays he should put something in front of his face, and if he can find nothing he should set up his stick; but if he has no stick with him he should draw a line, then what passes in front of him will not harm him.” \n\nAbu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 730"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He told that a man presented God’s Messenger with a slave called Mid'am, and while Mid'am was unsaddling a camel belonging to God’s Messenger he was struck by a random arrow which killed him. The people said, “Congratulations to him! He will go to paradise;” but God’s Messenger said, “Not at all. By Him in whose hand my soul is, the cloak he took on the day of Khaibar from the spoils which was not among the shares divided will blaze with fire upon him.” When the people heard that, a man brought a sandal-strap, or two sandal-straps, to the Prophet and said, “A sandal-strap of fire,” or, “Two sandal-straps of fire.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3834"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira said that when the Prophet once visited Bilal and saw he had a heap of dates, he asked him what it was. One his replying, “It is something I have stored up for tomorrow,” he said, “Are you not afraid that tomorrow you may see on account of it steam in the fire of jahannam on the day of resurrection? Spend it, Bilal, and do not fear poverty from the Lord of the Throne.”\n\nBaihaqi transmitted it in Shu’ab al-iman.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1797"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ya'la b. Umayya reported God’s messenger as saying, “Storing up food to sell it at a high price in the sacred territory is a profanation of its sanctity.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2609"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “When you put on your clothes and when you perform ablution begin with the right side.” \n\nAhmad and Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 371"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Mu'awiya reported God’s Messenger as saying, “If you are put in a position of authority, Mu'awiya, fear God and act justly.” He said that he kept thinking he would be afflicted by a governorship in accordance with what the Prophet had said till it actually came true.\n\nAhmad. Baihaqi transmitted Mu‘awiya’s tradition in Dalail an-nubuwa.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3558"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Sakhr b. Wada'a al-Ghamidi reported God’s Messenger as saying, \"O God, bless my people in their early morning.” When he sent out a detachment or an army he sent them at the beginning of the day. Sakhr was a merchant, and he would send off his merchandise at the beginning of the day; and he became rich and had much wealth. \n\nTirmidhi, Abu Dawud and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3745"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Umar reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Should anyone fall asleep and fail to recite his portion of the Qur’an or a part of it, if he recites it between the dawn and the noon prayer it will be recorded for him as though he had recited it during the night.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1183"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Ayyub told that when God’s messenger ate or drank he said, “Praise be to God who has given food and drink, made it easy to swallow, and provided an exit for it.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4036"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God's Messenger as saying, “When a woman who has been called to come to her husband’s bed refuses and he spends the night angry, the angels curse her till the morning.” In a version by both of them he said, “By Him in whose hand my soul is, if any woman who has been called to come to her husband’s bed refuses, He who is in heaven is displeased with her till her t husband is pleased with her.”\n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3118"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas said God’s messenger forbade breathing or blowing into a vessel. \n\nAbu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4104"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Mujammi' b. Jariya said:

Khaibar was divided among those who had been at al-Hudaibiya, and God’s Messenger divided it into eighteen portions. The army was one thousand five hundred of which three hundred were cavalry, and he gave two shares to a horseman and one to a footman. Abu Dawud transmitted it, saying Ibn ‘Umar’s tradition1 is sounder, and it is the one which is followed. The error in the tradition of Mujammi’ was because he said three hundred horsemen when there were only two hundred.
Habib b. Maslama al-Fihri said he saw the Prophet give a quarter of the spoil on the outward journey and a third on the return journey.2 

1. I have available two editions of Abu Dawud’s Sunan (Cairo, 1280 and 1348 A .H.). Both give Ibn Mu'awiya in place of Ibn 'Umar. See Jihad, 144.
2. This tradition and the following one are explained as referring to a section of the army which comes in contact with the enemy. The greater amount granted them when this happens on the return journey is because there is more difficulty and danger in fighting after having gone through the campaign. The second tradition is more explicit by making it clear that the fifth was deducted.

Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3843"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Sa'd b. Abu Waqqas reported God’s messenger as saying, “It is a fine thing when a believer praises and thanks God if good comes to him, and praises God and shows endurance if smitten by affliction. ' The believer is rewarded for everything, even for the morsel he raises to his wife’s mouth.”(The idea of the tradition is that by virtue of his faith the believer receives a reward for all his actions, none being too insignificant)\n\nBaihaqi transmitted it in Shu'ab al-iman.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1647"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Haritha b. Wahb told that God's messenger exhorted the people to give sadaqa, for the time was coming when a man would go with his sadaqa and find no one to accept it. A man would say, “If you had brought it yesterday I would have accepted it, but I have no need of it today.\" \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1778"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas told that dates were steeped for God’s messenger at the beginning of the night and he would drink it in the morning and the night after, the following day and the night after, and the next day up to the afternoon. If anything remained, he gave it to the servant to drink, or gave orders and it was poured out. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4115"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Al-Bara’ b. ‘Azib told that the Prophet forbade red saddle-cloths. It is transmitted in Sharh as-sunna.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4175"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"He reported God’s messenger as saying, 
“If anyone contributes a pair of anything in God’s path he will be invited to enter by the gates of paradise, for paradise has gates. Those who engage in prayer will be invited to enter by the gate of prayer; those who take part in jihad will be invited to enter by the gate of jihad; those who give sadaqa will be invited to enter by the gate of sadaqa; and those who fast will be invited to enter by the gate ar-Rayyan.”* Abu Bakr said, “No distress will rest on him who is invited to enter by those gates,** but will anyone be invited to enter by all those gates?” He replied, “Yes, and I hope you may be one.” 

(Bukhari and Muslim.)

* This word means literally 'well-watered,’ or 'fresh’.
** This is explained as meaning ‘by one of those gates,’as one who enters by any gate will get into paradise","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1802"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"'A'isha told that when she was with God's Messenger on a journey she raced him on foot and beat him, but when she grew she raced him and he beat her. He said, “This makes up for that beating.\" \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3123"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn 'Abbas said God’s messenger was lowered gently into the grave head first. \n\nShafi'i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1619"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, 
“Forgiveness was granted to an unchaste woman who coming upon a dog panting and almost dead with thirst at the mouth of a well, took off her shoe, tied it with her head-covering, and drew some water for it. On that account she was forgiven.” He was asked whether people received a reward for what they did to animals, and replied, “A reward is given in connection with every living creature.”*

(Bukhari and Muslim.)

* Literally, everything possessed of a moist liver.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1813"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Al-‘Irbad b. Sariya told that God’s messenger invited him to a meal shortly before dawn in Ramadan saying, “Come to the blessed morning meal.” \n\nAbu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1906"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas said that when the Prophet came to Mina he went to the jamra and threw pebbles at it, after which he went to his lodging in Mina and sacrificed his victim. He then called for a barber, and turning his right side to him, he let him shave him. He then called Abu Talha al-Ansari and gave him what had been shaved off; after which he turned his left side telling the barber to shave him, and when he had done so he gave Abu Talha what had been shaved off and told him to divide it among the people. \n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2538"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"l-Gharif b. ‘Ayyash ad-Dailami 1 said:

We went to Wathila b. al-Asqa‘ and said, “Tell us a tradition which has no addition or omission.” He replied angrily, “One of you recites when his copy of the Qur’an is hung up in his house, and he makes additions and omissions.” We declared that all we meant was a tradition he had heard from the Prophet, and he said they had gone to God’s Messenger about a friend of theirs who deserved (i.e., hell) for murder, 2 and he replied, “If you emancipate a slave on his behalf God will set free from hell a member of the body for every member of his.” 
Abu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it.

1. Mirqat, iii, 540 gives al-Gharif ad-Dailami but says it should correctly be Ibn ad-Dailami. It adds that Hakim in his Mustadrak says al-Gharif was a laqab of ‘Abdallah b. ad-Dailami, and that in Jami'-al-usul the name is given as al-Gharif b. ‘Ayyash ad-Dailami. This is the form in the Damascus edn. of the Mishkat, the one used in the translation above. It is also given by Ibn Hajar, Tahdhib, viii, 245.
2. Mirqat, iii, 541 suggests that the reference may be to someone who had killed a man unintentionally.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Emancipation · Hadith 3252"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He said that God’s messenger was asked what action was most excellent and replied that it was faith in God and His messenger. He was asked what came next and replied that it was jihad in God’s path. He was asked what came next and replied that it was a pilgrimage which was accepted. \n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2399"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Uqba b. ‘Āmir reported God’s messenger as saying, “He who recites the Qur’ān loudly is like him who gives sadaqa openly, and he who recites the Qur’ān quietly is like him who gives sadaqa secretly.” \n\nTirmidhī, Abū Dāwūd and Nasā’i transmitted it, Tirmidhī saying this is a hasan gharīb tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Excellent Qualities of the Qur'an · Hadith 2105"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Sahl b. Sa'd reported God’s messenger as saying, \"In paradise there are eight gates among which is a gate called ar-Rayyan which only those who fast will enter.\"\n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1867"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Yusuf b. ‘Abdallah b. Salam said he saw the Prophet take a piece of barley bread and put a date on it. Saying, “This is the condiment of this,” he ate it. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4051"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri reported God’s Messenger as  saying, “No prayer is to be said after the morning prayer until the sun rises, or after the afternoon prayer until the sun sets.”. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 980"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas said that God’s messenger and his companions performed an ‘umra from al-Ji'rana (A place where there was water less than half way from Mecca to at-Ta’if) and ran three times round the House. They put their upper garments under their armpits and threw the ends over their left shoulders. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2476"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
