data: {"body":"‘A'isha said Quraish were anxious about the Makhzumi woman who had committed theft and asked, “Who will speak to God’s Messenger about her?” Then they said, “Who will be bold enough for it but Usama b. Zaid, God’s Messenger’s friend?” So Usama spoke to him and God’s Messenger said, “Are you interceding regarding one of the punishments prescribed by God?” He then got up and gave an address, saying, “What destroyed your predecessors was just that when a person of rank among them committed a theft they left him alone, but when a weak one of their number committed a theft they inflicted the prescribed punishment on him. I swear by God that if Fatima daughter of Muhammad should steal I would have her hand cut off.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim). In a version by Muslim she said that a Makhzumi woman used to borrow goods and deny having received them, so the Prophet gave orders that her hand should be cut off. Her family went and spoke to Usama and he spoke about her to God's Messenger. Then he mentioned the tradition in similar form to what has preceded.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prescribed Punishments · Hadith 3461"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir reported the Prophet as saying, “Any slave who marries without his master's permission is a fornicator.” \n\nTirmidhi, Abu Dawud and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Marriage · Hadith 3009"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"She told that she had screened a store-room of hers with a curtain on which there were figures and the Prophet tore it down ; so she made two cushions out of it and had them in the house for sitting on.” \n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4306"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa'id said that in the time of the Prophet a man suffered loss affecting fruits he had bought and owed a large debt, so God’s messenger told the people to give him sadaqa and they did so, but as that was not enough to pay the debt in full God’s Messenger said to his creditors, “Take what you can find, but that is all you may have.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2780"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas told that the people were departing in all directions, so God’s messenger said, “None of you must go off till his obligations at the House are complete, except that this is remitted for a woman who is in her courses.” \n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2556"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Ja'far said the Prophet used to wear a signet-ring on his right hand. \nIbn Majah transmitted it, and Abu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it on ‘Ali’s authority.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4208"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas reported God’s messenger as saying, “He who goes out in\nsearch of knowledge is in God’s path till he returns.” Tirmidhi and\nDarimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Knowledge · Hadith 210"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"‘Abdallah b. Mas'ud said:

We used to greet the Prophet while he was engaged in prayer and he would respond to our greeting, but when we returned from the Negus* we greeted him and he did not respond to us, so we said, “Messenger of God, we used to greet you when you were engaged in prayer and you would respond to us.” He replied, “Prayer demands one’s whole attention.” 

* The reference is to the return of those who had gone from Mecca to Abyssinia when Muslims were being persecuted.

(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 922"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ali reported that a man came to the Prophet and said, “I washed because of sexual defilement, then prayed the dawn prayer but noticed a spot about the size of a nail which had not been touched by the water.” God’s messenger replied, “If you had rubbed your hand over it, it would have been enough for you.” \n\nIbn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 416"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abd Sa'id al-Khudri said that God’s messenger cursed the wailing-woman and the woman who listens to her. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1646"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “If I were invited to eat a trotter I would accept the invitation, and if I were presented with a fore-leg I would accept it.” \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1741"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that God’s Messenger used to raise his hands opposite his shoulders when he began prayer and when he said the takbir before bowing; and when he raised his head after bowing he raised them in the same way and said, “God listens to him who praises Him. To Thee, our Lord, be the praise!” But he did not do that when he prostrated himself. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 742"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Sa'id b. Sa'd b. ‘Ubada told that Sa'd b. ‘Ubada brought the Prophet a man deficient in build and sick, a member of the clan, who had been found in the act of having illicit intercourse with a slave woman of theirs. The Prophet said, “Get for him a stalk of the raceme of a palm-tree with a hundred twigs and strike him once.” \n\nIt is transmitted in Sharh as-sunna; and there is something similar in Ibn Majah’s version.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prescribed Punishments · Hadith 3430"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar reported God’s messenger as saying, “Only he who has no portion in the next world wears silk in this world.\" \n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4140"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that when the Prophet came to Mecca he entered it at the upper end and went out at the lower. \n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2453"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Khallad b. as-Sa’ib on his father’s authority reported God’s messenger as saying, “Gabriel came to me and commanded me to order my companions to raise their voices in the talbiya.” (The tradition ends by saying they were to raise their voices bil-ihlal au at-talbiya. These are alternative words meaning the same thing, and therefore I have not given any alternative in the translation)\n\nMalik, Tirmidhi, Abd Dawud, Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2440"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar reported God’s messenger as saying, \"When the cloth is set down a man must not get up till it is removed, nor must he withdraw his hand even if he has had enough till the people have finished, but if he does he should make his excuse, for that embarrasses his companion and he does not stretch out his hand although he may perhaps require the food.\" \n\nIbn Majah and Baihaqi, in Shu'ab al-iman, transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4082"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas reported God’s messenger as saying, “When a man is placed in his grave and his friends leave him, he hears the beat of their sandals. Then two angels come to him and, having made him sit up, they say, ‘What was your opinion of this man, of Muhammad?’ The believer replies, ‘I testify that he is God’s servant and messenger.’ He is then told to look at his abode in hell for which God has substituted for him an abode in paradise, and he sees them both. The hypocrite and infidel are asked, ‘What was your opinion of this man?’ and reply, ‘I do not know; I held the opinion others held.’ They will retort, ‘You neither knew nor did you follow .’ He will then be given a blow with iron hammers and will utter a shout which will be heard by all who are near him, with the exception of men and jinn.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim. The wording is Bukhari’s.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 119"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “When one of you makes a good profession of Islam, every good deed he does will be recorded for him ten to seven hundredfold, and every evil deed he does will be recorded as it is till he meets God.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 40"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"As-Sa’ib b. Yazid told that the Prophet wore two coats of mail at the battle of Uhud as a double protection. \n\nAbu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3723"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that his father ‘Umar b. al-Khattab used to pray during the night what God wished, then during the latter part of the night he woke his family for prayer saying to them, “Come to prayer.” Then he would recite this verse, “And command your family to observe the prayer, and be constant in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide you, and the issue pertains to piety” (Al-Qur'an; 20:132).\n\nMalik transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1176"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Wa’il b. Hujr told that Salama b. Yazid al-Ju‘fi questioned God’s Messenger saying, “Prophet of God, tell us what you command us to do if commanders arise over us who demand of us what is due to them and refuse us what is due to us.” He replied, “Listen and obey, for they are responsible only for what has been laid on them (cf. Al-Qur’an, 24:54) and you for what has been laid on you.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3517"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas reported God’s messenger as saying, “Let him who
interprets the Qur’an in the light of his opinion come to his abode
in hell.” A version has, “Let him who interprets the Qur’an without
knowledge come to his abode in hell.” Tirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Knowledge · Hadith 219"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Shariq al-Hauzani told that he visited ‘A’isha and asked her what God’s Messenger said first when he rose during the night. Replying that he had asked her a question she had never been asked by anyone before, she said that when he rose during the night he said “God is most great” ten times, “Praise be to God” ten times, “Glory be to God, and praise be to him” ten times, “Glory be to the King most holy” ten times, he asked pardon from God ten times, said “There is no god but God” ten times, then said, “O God, I seek refuge in Thee from the distress of this world and from the distress of the day of resurrection” ten times, then he began the prayer. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1153"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Umama reported God’s messenger as saying, “He who is not prevented from performing the pilgrimage by an obvious necessity, a tyrannical ruler, or a disease which confines him at home and dies without having performed the pilgrimage, may die if he wishes as a Jew, or if he wishes as a Christian.” \n\nDarimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2426"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that God’s messenger used to say, “O God, I seek refuge in Thee from the evil of what I have done and from the evil of what I have not done.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2356"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Al-Mughira b. ‘Shu'ba said:

I was a guest one night along with God's messenger and he ordered a haunch to be roasted, then took a broad knife and began to cut off slices for me. Bilal then came to tell him the time for prayer had come, and he threw down the knife saying, “What is the m atter with him! May his hands be covered with dust!”* My moustache was long, so he said, “I shall clip it for you over a tooth-stick,” or, “Clip it over a tooth-stick.”
*Taribat yadahu. I have here translated the phrase literally, but cf. p. 658. It is not normally to be taken literally. In this tradition the Prophet is evidently displeased because the call to prayer has been made so soon, but it should not be understood that he is calling down a curse on Bilal. In its use here it may indicate some degree of displeasure, but nothing more.

Tirmidhi transmitted it*","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4064"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that a client of God’s Messenger died leaving some property, but no relative or child, and God’s Messenger said, “Give what he has left to a man belonging to his village.\" \n\nAbu Dawud and Tirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Inheritance and Wills · Hadith 2931"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Umar said, “I held an administrative post in the time of God's Messenger, and he gave me payment for it.\" \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3591"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Sa'id b. al-Musayyib told that ‘Umar b. al-Khattab killed five or seven people for one man whom they had killed treacherously, ‘Umar saying. “If the people of San'a’ had conspired against him I would have killed them all.” \n\nMalik transmitted it, and Bukhari transmitted something similar on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Retaliation · Hadith 3341"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Uqba b. ‘Amir said that God’s Messenger was presented with a silk gown which he put on and wore while praying. Then when he withdrew he pulled it off vigorously as though he disapproved of it, saying, “This is not fitting for the pious.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 708"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Al-Muhajir b. Qunfudh said that he came upon the Prophet when he was passing water and saluted him, but he did not respond to the salutation till he had performed ablution. He then made his excuse to him saying, “I dislike mentioning God's name except when I am in a state of purity.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it. Nasa’i transmitted it up to “till he had performed ablution” and said, “then when he had performed ablution he responded to it.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 434"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that Quraish and those who followed their religion used to stand at al-Muzdalifa, and they were called al-Hums,(The plural of ahmas, meaning hardy or rigorous. It is said that this name was applied to them because they boasted of their bravery and endurance. Another explanation is that they observed rites of standing only at Hamss', which is the Ka’ba) but the rest of the Arabs used to stand at ‘Arafa ; then when Islam came God most high commanded His Prophet to go to ‘Arafat (Both 'Arafa and its plural‘Arafat are used. It is rather peculiar to find bcth used In the same tradition) and stand there, then go quickly from it. That is in accordance with the words of Him who is great and glorious, “Then go quickly from where the people went quickly.”(Qur’an, 2, 199)\n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2491"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He said, on his father’s authority, that his grandfather told that God’s Messenger gave judgment that a third of the blood wit should be paid for loss of eyesight when the eye is not removed. \n\nAbu Dawud and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Retaliation · Hadith 3360"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Mu'adh reported the Prophet as saying, “Seek refuge in God from covetousness which leads to disgrace.” \n\nAhmad and Baihaqi, in  ad-Da'awat al-kabir, transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2367"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Musa reported the Prophet as saying, “No affliction great or small afflicts a man but for a sin, but there are more which God forgives.” Then he recited, “Whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have done; but He forgives much.”(Qur’an, xlii, 30)\n\nTirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1478"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Humaid as-Sa‘idi said that when some people asked God’s Messenger how they should invoke blessings on him he told them to say, “O God, bless Muhammad, his wives and his offspring as Thou didst bless Abraham; and grant favours to Muhammad, his wives and his offspring as Thou didst grant favours to the family of Abraham. Thou art indeed praiseworthy and glorious.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 864"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He said that the Prophet used to fast on Mondays and Thursdays, and when someone remarked on this to him he said, “On Monday and Thursday God forgives every Muslim except two who are at variance, for He says they must be left till they make peace with one another.”\n\nAhmad and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1981"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Mas'ud reported God’s messenger as saying, “If anyone is predeceased by three of his children who did not grow old enough to sin, they will be a strong protection for him from hell.” When Abu Dharr said he had been predeceased by two, he told him that the same applied. Ubayy b. Ka'b Abu Mundhir, the chief of the Qur'an readers, said he had been predeceased by one, and he told him the same applied. \n\nTirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted it, Tirmidhi saying that this is a gharib tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1669"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Umar said that God's Messenger forbade the sale of fruits till they were clearly in good condition, forbidding it both to the seller and to the buyer. A version by Muslim says he forbade selling palm-trees (i.e. their fruit) till the dates began to ripen, and ears of corn till they were white and were safe from blight.\n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2721"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Umama reported God’s messenger as saying, “Gabriel never came to me without ordering me to use the tooth-stick, with the result that I have been afraid of chafing the front of my mouth.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 358"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that when ‘Umar consulted the Prophet about a vow he had made in the pre-Islamic period to spend a night in devotion in the sacred mosque, he said, “Fulfill your vow.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 2007"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Mas'ud reported God’s Messenger as saying, “No man who acquires unlawful property and gives some of it in alms will have it accepted from him; neither will he receive a blessing for it if he con-tributes some of it; and if he leaves some of it behind him (i.e. when he dies) it will be his provision for hell. God does not obliterate an evil deed by an evil one, but He obliterates an evil deed by a good one. What is impure does not obliterate what is impure.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it, and the same is given in Sharh as-sunna.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2656"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abū Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “Would one of you like, when he returns to his family, to find there three large, fat pregnant she-camels? When we replied that we would, he said, “Three verses which one of you recites in his prayer are better for him than three large, fat, pregnant she-camels.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Excellent Qualities of the Qur'an · Hadith 2016"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that when God’s messenger came to Mecca he went to the stone and touched it, then moved to his right, running three circuits and walking four. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2457"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that the dogs used to go here and there in the mosque in the time of God’s messenger and that they did not sprinkle any place where they had been. \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 476"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Qatada told that he saw a wild ass and killed it. The Prophet asked whether they had any of its flesh and when he replied that they had a leg he took it and ate it. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Game and Animals Which May Be Slaughtered · Hadith 3942"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Muhammad b. Qais b. Makhrama said that God’s messenger addressed the people as follows, “The people of pre-Islamic times used to return from 'Arafa when the sun before setting was shining in their faces like men’s turbans, and from al-Muzdalifa after the sun rose when it was shining in their faces like men’s turbans; (When the sun is low it shines only on men’s foreheads, and this is here likened to a turban) but we do not return from ‘Arafa till the sun sets, and we return from al-Muzdalifa before the sun rises. Our guidance differs from that of the worshippers of idols and those who attribute partners to God.”\n\nBaihaqi transmitted it in Shu'ab al-iman, saying “He addressed us . . .” and then going on, with the tradition to similar effect.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2501"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Qatada told that when God's Messenger encamped at night on a journey he lay down on his right side, and when he encamped a little before morning he raised his forearm and placed his head on the palm of his hand. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3759"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Make things easy and do not make them difficult; make people calm and do not scare them.’’ \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3566"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “None of you will be rescued by his works.” He was asked if not even he would, and replied, “Not even I unless God covers me with His mercy; but if you keep to the straight path, are moderate, pray morning and evening and part of the night, and earnestly practise moderation, you will reach .” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2268"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas said, “When we prayed behind the Prophet at midday in summer we prostrated ourselves on our clothing to protect ourselves from the heat.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim, the wording being Bukhari’s.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 546"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn Mas'ud said, ‘If anyone follows someone’s custom let him follow the custom of one who is dead, for one cannot be sure of the living not being led astray. Those to follow are Muhammad’s Companions who were the most excellent among the people, purest in heart, most profound in knowledge, most unassuming, whom God chose for companionship with His Prophet and to establish His religion. So recognise their excellence, follow their traces, and hold as fast as you can to their character and way of life, for they followed right guidance.” \n\nRazin transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 184"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “The religion will continue to prevail as long as people hasten to break the fast, because the Jews and the Christians delay doing so.” \n\nAbu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1904"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “Every prophet has a supplication which receives an answer, but whereas every prophet made his supplication in this world, I have kept mine till the day of resurrection to be used in intercession for my people, and if God will, it will reach those of my people who have died without associating anything with God.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it, and Bukhari has a shorter version.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2126"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"‘A’isha said:

God’s messenger recited, “He it is who has sent down to you the Book in which are fundamental verses” going on to “no one takes warning but those of insight.”1 She reported God’s messenger as saying, “When you (using the feminine singular pronoun whereas Muslim has the masculine plural) see those who study what is dubious in it, those are they whom God named, so be on your guard against them.” 

(Bukhari and Muslim.)

1 Quran, iii, 7.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 144"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira said that the Prophet visited his mother’s grave and wept and caused those around him to weep. He then said, \"I asked my Lord's permission to pray for forgiveness for her, but I was not allowed; I then asked His permission to visit her grave and I was allowed; so visit graves, for they make one mindful of death.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1677"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that when God’s messenger intended to perform the pilgrimage he made proclamation among the people and they assembled. Then when he came to al-Baida’ (a place near Dhul Hulaifa) he put on the ihram. \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2444"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Asma’ daughter of ‘Umais said she told God’s messenger that Fatima daughter of Abu Hubaish had had a flow of blood for a certain period and had not prayed. God’s messenger said, “Glory be to God! This comes from the devil. She should sit in a tub, and when she sees yellowness appearing on the top of the water she should wash once for the noon and afternoon prayer, once for the sunset and night prayer, once for the dawn prayer, and in between times she should perform ablution.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it, saying Mujahid transmitted from Ibn ‘Abbas that when the washing became too much for her be ordered her to combine the two prayers.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 521"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas said that the Prophet married Maimuna when he was on pilgrimage. \n\nBukhari and Muslim.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2569"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Thauban reported God’s Messenger as saying, “There are three things which are unlawful for anyone to do. A man must not act as imam for others in prayer and make a supplication for himself excluding them, for if he does that he has acted treacherously towards them. No one must look inside a house before asking permission to enter, for if he does so he has acted treacherously towards . And no one should pray while retaining urine, but should first relieve himself.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it, and Tirmidhi has something similar.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1009"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira said that a man asked the Prophet whether one who was fasting might embrace his wife and he gave him permission, but when another came to him and asked him he forbade him. The one to whom he gave permission was an old man and the one whom he forbade was a youth.\n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1915"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Yahya b. Abd ar-Rahman said that ‘Umar went out with a party of riders among whom was ‘Amr b al-‘As. When they came to a cistern and ‘Amr asked its owner whether beasts of prey came down to it, ‘Umar said, “Don't tell us, owner of the cistern, for we go down to what beasts of prey leave, and they go down to what we leave.”\n\nMalik transmitted it and Razin made an addition saying that some transmitters add to ‘Umar’s words that he said he had heard God’s messenger say, “They have in their bellies what they have taken, and what remains is pure for us and drinkable.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 451"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Abu Sa'id reported God’s messenger as saying:

“If God were to withhold rain from his servants for five years and then send it, a section of mankind would be infidels saying they had been supplied with water through the agency of the rainy star al-Mijdah*.”

Nasa’i transmitted it.

* The word comet from a root meaning to stir up, and the plural is used as a general name for stars which are said to stir up rain, the singular used here may refer to the Hyades, but other explanations are also given. As rainy seasons were connected with particular times at which certain stars rose, the rain was attributed to them.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Medicine and Spells · Hadith 4407"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Zaid b Khalid al-Juhani reported God’s Messenger as saying, “If anyone observes two prostrations without being negligent in them, God will forgive him his previous sins.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 534"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa'id al-Khudri told that when God’s Messenger swore strongly he said, “No, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Abu Qasim.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Oaths and Vows · Hadith 3288"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Bilal b. ‘Abdallah b. ‘Umar on his father’s authority reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Do not prevent the women from their shares in the mosques when they ask your permission.” Bilal said, “I swear by God I will certainly prevent them.” ‘Abdallah replied, “I tell you that God’s Messenger said it, yet you say you will certainly prevent them!” In a version by Salim,* his father is reported as saying:

‘Abdallah confronted him, and reviling him in terms the like of which I have never heard at any other time, he said, “I give you information on the authority of God’s Messenger, yet you say, ‘I swear by God I will certainly prevent them’!” 

* He is Salim b. ‘Abdallah b. ‘Umar b. al-Khattab.

Muslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1021"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “Ramadan, a blessed month, has come to you during which God has made it obligatory for you to fast. In it the gates of heaven are opened, the gates of al-Jahim are locked, and the rebellious devils are chained. In it God has a night which is better than a thousand months. He who is deprived of its good has indeed suffered deprivation.\" \n\nAhmad and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1871"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ubayy b. Ka'b said, “Prayer in a single garment was a practice we followed along with God’s Messenger, and no blame was cast on us.” Ibn Mas'ud said, “That was only when clothing was scarce, but when God enlarged our circumstances prayer in two garments became purer.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 720"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said, “God’s Messenger sent me on some business, and when I came to him he was praying on his riding-beast towards the east and making the prostration lower than the bowing.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1274"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas reported God’s Messenger as saying on that day, meaning the day of Hunain, “He who kills an infidel gets what he takes from him.” Abu Talha killed twenty men that day and got what was taken from them. \n\nDarimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3839"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Anas said that the Prophet visited Umm Sulaim, and when she brought him some dates and clarified butter he said, “Put your butter back in its container and your dates in their vessel, for I am fasting.” He then went to a separate part of the house and prayed a prayer which was not one of the prescribed prayers, and invoked a blessing on Umm Sulaim and the inhabitants of her house. \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1984"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Hisham b. ‘Urwa, on his father’s authority, told that Hisham b. Hakim came upon some Nabataeans in Syria who had been made to stand in the sun with olive-oil poured over their heads. On his asking what the meaning of that was and being told that they were suffering punishment concerning the land-tax, Hisham said he could testify to having heard God’s Messenger say, “God will punish those who punish people in this world.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Retaliation · Hadith 3379"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ali reported God’s Messenger as saying, “When the middle night of Sha'ban comes, spend the night in prayer and fast during the day, for in it God most high comes down at sunset to the lowest heaven and says, ‘Is there no one who asks forgiveness so that I may forgive him ? Is there no one who asks provision so that I may provide him? Is there no one afflicted so that I may relieve him? Is there not such and such? Is there not such and such?’ till the dawn comes.” \n\nIbn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1239"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira told how on an occasion when God’s Messenger led them in the noon prayer, there was a man at the back of the rows who performed the prayer badly. When he had said the taslim God’s Messenger called out to him, “So and so, do you not fear God? Do you not see how you should pray? You people think that part of what you are doing is hidden from me, but I swear by God that I see behind me just as I see in front of me.\" \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 760"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Sarjis said that when God’s messenger went on a journey he sought refuge in God from the difficulty of the journey, sorrow when he returned, scarcity after abundance, the claim of the oppressed, and seeing harm come to his family and property. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2316"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ubada b. as-Samit reported God’s messenger as saying, “The first thing God created was the pen. He told it to write and when it asked Him what it should write He told it to write what was decreed, so it wrote what had taken place and what would take place to all eternity.” \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it, saying that this is a tradition whose isnad is gharib.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 88"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Wa’il b. Hujr said he saw that when God’s Messenger prostrated himself he got down on his knees before putting his hands on the ground, and when he got up he raised his hands before his knees. \n\nAbu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 843"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar reported God’s messenger as saying, “The woman who is menstruating and the one who is seminally defiled must not recite any of the Qur’an.” \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 428"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"An-Nu‘man b. Bashir reported God’s Messenger as saying, “From wheat wine is made, from barley wine is made, from dried dates wine is made, from raisins wine is made, and from honey wine is made.” \n\nTirmidhi, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it, Tirmidhi saying this is a gharib tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prescribed Punishments · Hadith 3493"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “Anyone who has washed a dead body must bathe himself.” \n\nIbn Majah transmitted it; and Ahmad, Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud added, “And he who carries it must perform ablution.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 500"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that God's Messenger forbade selling fruit years ahead, and commanded that unforeseen loss be remitted in respect of what is affected by blight. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Business Transactions · Hadith 2723"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said it was the Prophet’s custom not to go to sleep till he had recited “A. L. M The sending down,” (Qur’ān, 32) and “Blessed is He in whose hand is the kingdom.” \n\nAhmad, Tirmidhī and Dārimī transmitted it, Tirmidhī saying this is a sahīh tradition. The same is said in Sharh as-sunna, but in al-Masābīh it is called gharīb.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Excellent Qualities of the Qur'an · Hadith 2058"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"“Abdallah b. 'Amr said God’s messenger was never seen reclining while eating, nor walking with two men at his heels. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4040"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that the people tried to see the new moon and he informed God’s messenger that he had seen it, so he fasted and commanded the people to observe the fast.\" \n\nAbu Dawud and Darimi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1888"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jarir b. ‘Abdallah reported God’s messenger as saying, “When the collector of sadaqa comes to you see that he is pleased with you when he leaves you.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Zakat · Hadith 1690"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Anas said:

When we encamped we did not glorify God* till we had loosened the saddles. 

* This is explained as meaning to perform the salat. Cf. Mirqat, iv, 218.

Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3754"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “Avoid the seven noxious things.\" When his hearers asked, “What are they, messenger of God?\" he replied, “Associating anything with God, magic, killing one whom God has declared inviolate without a just cause, devouring usury, consuming the property of an orphan, turning back when the army advances, and slandering chaste women who are believers but indiscreet.\" \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 47"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"As-Sa‘b b. Jaththama told that God’s Messenger was asked about the polytheists whose settlements were attacked at night when some of their women and offspring were smitten, and replied that they were of their number. A version has it that they were regarded in the same way as their parents. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3780"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha said that God’s Messenger used to pray sitting, and would recite the Qur’an while sitting; then when about thirty or forty verses of his recitation remained he stood up and recited while standing. Then he bowed, then he prostrated himself, and after that he did the same kind of thing in the second rak'a. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1215"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s messenger as saying, “If anyone
acquires knowledge of things by which God’s good pleasure is sought,
but acquires it only to get some worldly advantage, he will not experience the ‘arf, i.e. the odour, of paradise on the day of resurrection.”
Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Knowledge · Hadith 215"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Amr b. al-‘As said that the Prophet mentioned prayer one day saying, “If anyone keeps to it, it will be light, evidence and salvation for him on the day of resurrection; but if anyone does not keep to it, it will not be for him light, evidence, or salvation, and on the day of resurrection he will be associated with Qarun, Pharaoh, Haman, 1 and Ubayy b. Khalaf”2 

1. These three are mentioned together in Al-Qur’an, 29:39; 40:24. A longer account is given of Qarun in 28:76 ff. Haman is mentioned also in 28:38. The Old Testament gives the story of Korah (Qarun) in Numbers, Chap. 16, and of Haman in Esther, Chaps, 3 ff.
2. Ubayy had been an enemy of the Prophet in Mecca. Ubayy had said he would kill him, but the Prophet replied that if God willed he would kill Ubayy. At the battle of Uhud (3 A H.) Ubayy received a scratch, and remembering the Prophet’s words, he felt sure he was going to die. He died at Sarif, about six miles from Mecca, as he was returning home. See the Cairo edition of as-Sira an-nabawiya by Ibn Hisham, 1355/1936, vol.3, p. 89.

Ahmad, Darimi, and Baihaqi in Shu'ab al-lman transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 535"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira told of hearing God’s messenger state that God most high says, “Who is more in the wrong than he who sets about creating things like what I have created ? Well, let such people create an atom, let them create a grain, or a grain of barley.” \n(Bukhari and Muslim).","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4309"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said they were forbidden game caught by a dog belonging to Magians. \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Game and Animals Which May Be Slaughtered · Hadith 3920"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Sa'id reported God’s Messenger as saying, “The one who will be dearest to God and nearest to Him in station of the day of resurrection will be a just imam, and the one who will be most hateful to God on the day of resurrection and will receive the severest punishment (or as a version has, will be farthest from Him in station) will be a tyrannical imam.” \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it, saying this is a hasan gharib tradition.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3548"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar told that God’s Messenger allotted three portions for a man and his horse, one for him and two for his horse. \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3824"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Amr reported God’s Messenger as saying, “When one of you breaks wind when he has sat at the end of his prayer before giving the salutation, his prayer is valid.” \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it saying that this is a tradition whose isnad is not strong, and there is confusion about its isnad.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 949"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A'isha said that the Prophet did not awake after sleeping by night or by day without using the tooth-stick before performing ablution.\n\nAhmad and Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 355"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira said that God’s messenger forbade uninterrupted fasting, and when a man said, “You fast uninterruptedly, messenger of God,” he replied, “Which of you is like me? During the night my Lord gives me food and drink.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1895"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He said that God’s messenger said to an invalid whom he visited, \"Cheer up, for God most high says, ‘It is my fire to which I give power over my believing servant in the world to be his portion of hell on the day of resurrection.” \n\nAhmad, Ibn Majah and Baihaqi, in Shu'ab al- iman, transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Funerals · Hadith 1504"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Rafi' b. Khadij said that in the division of the booty God’s Messenger used to treat ten sheep as equivalent to a camel.\n\nNasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3867"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"'Abdallah b. ‘Umar told of the vision the Prophet had about Medina. He said, “I saw a black woman with dishevelled hair go out of Medina and settle at Mahya'a, and interpreted it as meaning that the pestilence of Medina had been transferred to Mahya'a, which is al-Juhfa.” \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Rites of Pilgrimage · Hadith 2621"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn Abbas said God’s messenger prohibited every beast of prey with a fang and every bird with a talon. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Game and Animals Which May Be Slaughtered · Hadith 3939"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"She also reported God’s messenger as saying, “When the parts which are circumcised pass one another washing is necessary,” adding that God’s messenger and she did that, and then washed. \n\nTirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 409"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that he heard the Prophet say, “When the devil hears the summons to prayer he goes off till he is as far away as ar-Rauha’.” The transmitter said that ar-Rauha’ is thirty-six miles from Medina. \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 627"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu' Musa reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Every eye is adulterous, and when a woman perfumes herself and passes a company, she is such and such meaning adulterous. \n\nTirmidhi transmitted it, and Abu Dawud and Nasa’i have something similar.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1004"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ali reported God’s messenger as saying, “God loves the believing servant who is severely tried and is penitent.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Supplications · Hadith 2257"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas reported the Prophet as saying, “If people were given what they asked when they brought a case some would claim the lives and property of others; but the oath must be taken by the defendant.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it. In the commentary on his work by Nawawi it says that in Baihaqi’s version with an isnad which is hasan or sahih there is an addition on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas which is traced to the Prophet, “But the proof lies on the plaintiff and the oath must be taken by him who rejects the claim.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: The Offices of Commander and Qadi · Hadith 3598"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"He reported the Prophet as saying, “God has cursed men who imitate women and women who imitate men.” \nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4244"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Suwaid b. Wahb quoted a son of a Companion of God’s messenger who said his father reported God’s messenger as saying, “He who gives up wearing beautiful garments when he is able to do so (out of humility, as is stated in a version) will be clothed by God with the robe of honour, and he who marries for God's sake will be crowned by God with the crown of the kingdom.” \nAbu Dawud transmitted it, and Tirmidhi transmitted the tradition about the clothing on Suwaid’s authority on the authority of Mu'adh b. Anas.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Clothing · Hadith 4166"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. ‘Amr said, “If anyone invokes blessing on the Prophet once God and His angels will grant him seventy blessings.” \n\nAhmad transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 879"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar said that when the Muslims came to Medina they gathered and sought to know the time of prayer, but no one summoned them. One day they discussed the matter, and one of them said, “Use something like the bell of the Christians.\" Another said, “Use a horn like that of the Jews.\" But when ‘Umar said, “I suggest that you send a man to announce the prayer,\" God’s Messenger said, “Get up, Bilal, and summon to prayer.\" \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 602"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Abdallah b. Zaid said that God’s messenger performed the details of ablution twice each, and said, “It was a light upon a light.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 391"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A’isha reported God’s messenger as saying, “When one of you eats and forgets to mention God over his food he should say, ‘In the name of God at the beginning and at the end of it’.” \n\nTirmidhi and Abu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Foods · Hadith 4032"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Buraida told of a man asking God’s Messenger about the time of prayer, to which he replied, “Pray with us these two,” meaning two days. When the sun passed the meridian he gave command to Bilal who uttered the call to prayer, then he commanded him and he made the announcement declaring that the time to begin the noon prayer had come. He gave him command and he made the announcement declaring that the time to being the afternoon prayer had come when the sun was high, white and clear. Then he gave him command and he made the announcement declaring that the time to begin the sunset prayer had come when the sun had set. Then he gave him command and he made the announcement declaring that the time to begin the night prayer had come when the twilight had ended. Then he gave him command and he made the announcement declaring that the time to begin the dawn prayer had come when the dawn appeared. Next day he commanded him to delay the noon prayer till the extreme heat had passed and he did so, and he allowed it to be delayed till the extreme heat had passed. He observed the afternoon prayer when the sun was high, delaying it beyond the time he had previously observed it. He observed the sunset prayer before the twilight had ended; he observed the night prayer when a third of the night had passed; and he observed the dawn prayer when there was clear daylight. Then asking where the man was who had enquired about the time of prayer and receiving from him a reply that he was present, he said, “The time for your prayer is within the limits of what you have seen.” \n\nMuslim transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 539"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘A'isha reported God's messenger as saying, “Seek lailat al-qadr on an old number night among the last ten in Ramadan.” \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1990"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Umar reported God’s Messenger as saying, “Two characteristics are suspended on the necks of those who call the adhan for the Muslims, their fasting and their prayer.” \n\nIbn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 641"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Ali, Abud Darda’, Abu Huraira, Abu Umama, ‘Abdallah b. ‘Umar, ‘Abdallah b. ‘Amr, Jabir b. ‘Abdallah and ‘Imran b. Husain all reported God’s Messenger as saying, \"He who sends a contribution towards God’s path and stays in his house will have seven hundred dirhams for every dirham he contributes, but he who fights in person and contributes towards that expedition of his will have seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham he contributes.” Then he recited this verse, \"And God multiplies to whom He will.” (Al-Qur’an; 2:261)\n\nIbn Majah transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3694"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
Mishkat al-Masabih
data:
{"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas said:

God’s Messenger was a servant under command who applied to us* only three things which he did not apply to the people in general. He ordered us to perform ablution fully, not to consume sadaqa, and not to make an ass cover a mare. 

* He means the members of the Prophet’s family.

Tirmidhi and Nasa’i transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3719"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God's messenger as saying, “There are three signs of a hypocrite.” Muslim added, “Even if he fasts, prays, and asserts that he is a Muslim.” Thereafter both Bukhari and Muslim said, “When he speaks he lies, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays his trust.”","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Faith · Hadith 49"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Uqba b. ‘Amir said the Prophet gave him some goats to divide among his friends as sacrificial animals, and a yearling remained over. He mentioned it to God’s Messenger, and he said, \"Sacrifice it yourself.” In a version he said he told God’s Messenger he had got a lamb, and he replied, \"Sacrifice it.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1378"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Abu Huraira reported God’s Messenger as saying, “If anyone is in time for a rak‘a in the prayer along with the imam he has said the whole prayer.” \n\n(Bukhari and Muslim.)","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prayer · Hadith 1334"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"‘Umar b. al-Khattab told that a man called ‘Abdallah whose laqab was Ass used to make the Prophet laugh. The Prophet had beaten him because of wine-drinking, but when he was brought to him one day and he gave orders and had him beaten, and then one of those present said, “O God, curse him. How often he is brought!” he said, “Do not curse to him. I swear by God that for all I know he loves God and His messenger.\" \n\nBukhari transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Prescribed Punishments · Hadith 3472"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Jabir said that when the Prophet wished to relieve himself he went off where no one could see him. \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Purification · Hadith 319"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ruwaifi' b. Thabit reported the Prophet as saying, “He who believes in God and the last day must not ride a packhorse belonging to the booty of the Muslims and put it back when he has emaciated it; and he who believes in God and the last day must not wear a garment belonging to the booty of the Muslims and put it back when he has made it threadbare.” \n\nAbu Dawud transmitted it.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Jihad · Hadith 3855"}

title: Mishkat al-Masabih
data: {"body":"Ibn ‘Abbas said that when the month of Ramadan began God's messenger set every prisoner free and gave to every beggar.","book":"Mishkat al-Masabih","author":"Al-Khatib Al-Tabrizi","format":"prose","source":"Mishkat al-Masabih","reference":"Chapter: Fasting · Hadith 1875"}
